rounds.proof_sketch: inner_size=256, grid_y=ceil(256/256)=1, inner_idx=blockIdx.y*256+threadIdx.x ∈ [0,255]. The mutation changes behavior only when inner_idx==inner_size=256, but max(inner_idx)=255 < 256.
rounds.survival_reason: The mutation changes the early-return condition from >= to >, which only affects threads where inner_idx equals exactly inner_size. With fixed input shape [16,256,256] and dim=1, inner_size=256 and grid_y=1, so inner_idx ranges from 0 to 255. Since 255 < 256, no thread ever has inner_idx == inner_size, making the >= vs > distinction irrelevant. Both conditions evaluate to false for all threads, causing identical execution paths.
rounds.kill_strategy: Unkillable under fixed shapes. Would require inner_size not divisible by block_size (256), e.g., inner_size=257 would create grid_y=2 and allow inner_idx=256. But shape changes are prohibited.
rounds.recommendations: For mutation testing of boundary guards, ensure test configurations include cases where tensor dimensions are NOT exact multiples of block sizes. Consider parameterized shape testing or specific edge-case dimensions (e.g., 257, 255) to expose off-by-one boundary mutations.
